note: Tables with two or more CREATE TABLE definitions that cannot describe one table — each demands a NOT NULL column the other has no place for. D1 holds one table per name and every definition is IF NOT EXISTS, so the first to run wins and the rest are no-ops; the code written against the loser cannot insert a row. Which shape is live is NOT provable from this repository: top-level sql/*.sql files are applied by hand (scripts/migrate-d1.mjs enumerates only sql/migrations/*.sql), so file order does not settle it. Each entry records what IS provable — chiefly whether the worker's own writers agree with each other — and names the PRAGMA that would settle the rest. The gate fails on NEW entries and on entries here that no longer collide, so this list cannot go stale. Resolving one means converging the definitions and deleting its line.
resolve_with: npx wrangler d1 execute studioos-db --remote --command="PRAGMA table_info('<table>')"

tables.capital_calls: WRITERS DISAGREE. routes/legalcap.ts inserts (deal_id, syndicate_id, amount_cents, currency, …) against its own ensureSchema at legalcap.ts:72; routes/funds.ts and routes/capital.ts read WHERE limited_partner_id = ?, which is the shape sql/consolidate_capital_rebuild.sql builds (uid, limited_partner_id, lp_investor_id, project_id, amount REAL NOT NULL, …). No single table satisfies both: the rebuild shape has no deal_id or amount_cents, and requires amount + uid that legalcap never binds. At least one of the two capital-call paths is dead in production.
tables.metrics_snapshots: THREE INCOMPATIBLE WRITERS, at most one of which works: (scope, scope_id, metric_name, value[, extra]) per sql/infrastructure.sql; (project_id, snapshot_date, mrr, arr, monthly_churn_pct, active_users, source) per sql/schema.sql; and (deal_id, key_metrics, traction_score, created_by) per routes/pipeline.ts. Each names columns the others lack and omits NOT NULL columns the others require. Two of the three insert paths cannot be writing rows.
tables.calendar_events: WRITERS DISAGREE, and the evidence points one way. The (uid, user_id, source, external_uri, …) shape from sql/schema.sql and migration 018 is almost certainly live: routes/assistant.ts filters calendar_events WHERE user_id = ?, and user_id exists only in that shape. services/wellbeing/bookings.ts:248 declares a different table (kind, source_id, source_uid NOT NULL) and inserts against it at :267, so expert-booking rows are most likely never written — which matches that file's own header comment describing a calendar_events row it expects the webhook to write.
tables.service_offerings: The only INSERT in the worker names (uid, owner_user_id, title, category, summary, price_usd, …), the sql/schema.sql and migration 034 shape. sql/t13_t14_t15.sql:397 declares a marketplace variant requiring partner_id NOT NULL with no owner_user_id at all. If the t13 file was applied first, that INSERT cannot succeed.
tables.advisor_bookings: RESOLVED BY EVIDENCE, kept on record because the definitions still conflict. routes/advisors.ts inserts (uid, slot_id, advisor_id, founder_user_id, topic, notes, status, …) — the sql/t13_t14_t15.sql:52 shape — and that booking flow works, so sql/schema.sql:1002's six-column version requiring booker_user_id is the dead one. This is the worked example that the numbered file does not always win. services/calendar.ts was corrected to the t13 shape rather than schema.sql's.
tables.ic_meetings: routes/calendar.ts inserts (uid, title, agenda, start_at, duration_min, deal_id, organizer_user_id, location_kind, location_uri) — the sql/calendar.sql:19 shape, which requires start_at and organizer_user_id. sql/schema.sql:1010 and migration 034 declare a variant requiring starts_at instead. The worker's reads (ORDER BY start_at, SELECT organizer_user_id) agree with the writer, so calendar.sql's shape is the one the code assumes throughout.
tables.founder_checkins: routes/calendar.ts inserts (uid, founder_user_id, counterpart_user_id, project_id, title, notes, start_at, duration_min, location_kind, location_uri) — the sql/calendar.sql:58 shape. sql/schema.sql:1017 and migration 034 declare a variant requiring user_id, which no writer binds. As with ic_meetings the worker is internally consistent; only the schema files disagree.
tables.wellbeing_resources: FOUR definitions, two shapes. Both INSERTs in routes/wellbeing.ts name (uid, category, name, description, url, region, is_24_7, is_free, sort_order[, created_by_user_id]) — the sql/financials_wellbeing.sql:48 and migration 052 shape, matching routes/wellbeing.ts:104's own ensureSchema. sql/schema.sql:1038 and migration 034 declare a variant requiring title, which nothing writes. The writer side is consistent; the two schema files are the outliers.
